rulings.Calendar Matter: Notice Of Motion And Motion To Maintain Confidentiality Designation Of Videos Produced Under Protective Order; Memorandum Of Points And Authorities **Redcted**
rulings.Rulings: Set for Law and Motion/Discovery on Monday July 13, 2026, Line 7, 1-DEFENDANT WAYMO LLC's Motion To Maintain Confidentiality Designation Of Videos Produced Under Protective Order. Defendant Waymo LLC's motion to maintain the confidentiality designations of the videos produced under protective order is granted and its request for monetary sanctions is denied. Waymo met its burden of showing per the stipulated protective order that the videos that are the subject of this motion contain trade secret information and/or confidential, commercially sensitive proprietary information. The court credits the declaration of Chrix Finne which sufficiently establishes that the videos contain protectable information per the protective order. The Finne declaration is neither conclusory nor does it contradict Waymo's contention that the videos contain protectable information. While unsuccessful, plaintiff Jennifer Hanki's challenge to the designation of the videos was made in good cause based on her not unreasonable intuitive argument that the videos do not contain protectable information because the vehicles' cameras are visible by an external inspection of the vehicles. Because Hanki did not lack good cause for her challenge to the designation of the videos, Waymo's request for monetary sanctions is denied per the terms of the protective order. rulings.Rulings: Set for Law and Motion/Discovery on Monday July 13, 2026, Line 13, PLAINTIFF MYTHILY SIVARAJAH MOTION TO QUASH SUBPOENAS Plaintiff Mythily Sivarajah's motion to quash subpoenas is recharacterized as a motion for a protective order providing plaintiff a "first look" at the documents produced in response to the subpoenas and, as so characterized, the motion is granted and plaintiff's request for monetary sanctions is denied. Information about plaintiff's HIV status, sexual health including STI testing, and her OB/Gyn history is confidential and not discoverable absent a showing that plaintiff has waived her confidentiality as to this information or the information is directly relevant to one or more issues in the case. Defendants have not shown that plaintiff has waived her confidentiality as to this information or the information is directly relevant to one or more issues in the case. Thus the court adopts the plaintiff's "first look" approach. The deposition officer must deliver the responsive documents only to the plaintiff. The plaintiff must ensure that each page of the documents is bates-numbered or similarly labeled and make one full set of the responsive documents identified as the "court's set." No later than fifteen court days after receiving the responsive documents, plaintiff is required to produce all responsive documents to defendants less any redactions for information about plaintiff's HIV status, sexual health including STI testing, and her OB/Gyn history. Any redactions must be reflected in a redaction log delivered to defendants at the same time as the documents are produced to defendants. If the parties are unable to resolve any disagreements about the redactions after meeting and conferring, defendants may file a motion to compel production of some or all of the redacted information and, in that event, plaintiff must provide unredacted pages to the court for in camera review with her opposition papers to the motion. Because defendants acted with substantial justification, the plaintiff's request for monetary sanctions is denied. rulings.Rulings: Set for Law and Motion/Discovery on Monday July 13, 2026, Line 14, PLAINTIFF SEMIANALYSIS LLC A FLORIDA LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY's Motion To Compel Arbitration And To Stay Proceedings. Plaintiff Semianalysis, LLC's motion to compel arbitration and stay proceedings is granted and this case is stayed pending completion of arbitration proceedings on the claims alleged in both the complaint and cross-complaint and the defenses alleged thereto. The order filed in case 635375 on May 19, 2026 resolves this motion. That order addressed all or substantially all of the issues raised by the parties in support of and opposition to this motion. Defendant Wei Zhou's opposition papers to this motion are the functional equivalent of a motion to reconsider the May 19, 2026 order without identifying any new or different facts, circumstances or law that supports or require a different result. Now that the time has passed to seek reconsideration of the May 19, 2026 order, Wei Zhou's remedy if he disagrees with that order is to seek appellate review, not a contrary order from this court.
